findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — `guests[]` has no size bound and the mutation has no rate limit

- One authenticated request can create an unbounded number of attendee rows and send an unbounded number of emails from the Cal.com sending domain. `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` declares neither `.min()` nor `.max()`, and no `checkRateLimitAndThrowError` guards the procedure. Any user who is merely an attendee on a booking can drive it. The cost is domain-reputation damage and a provider-side attendee-cap rejection on the calendar side. Fix: `.min(1).max(10)` on the schema plus a per-user rate limit. The cap value is a product choice -- 10 is the reviewers' defensible default; tune it to whatever booking creation already allows. Severity note: security called this P0, performance and adversarial called it P1. Kept at P0 because the fix is two lines and the abuse path needs no privilege beyond being on the invite.

- Event types that opted out of standard emails still get add-guests mail. `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)` is the only sender in `email-manager.ts` that takes no `eventTypeMetadata`; its immediate sibling `sendLocationChangeEmails` gates both the organizer push and the attendee fan-out behind `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` at lines 503 and 515. Fix: add the parameter, wrap both pushes, and pass `booking.eventType?.metadata` from the handler. Five reviewers agreed independently.

- On a team booking, no team member is notified. The `evt` literal at lines 124-147 never assigns `team`, so the `if (calendarEvent.team?.members)` loop at `email-manager.ts:531-537` is dead for this caller. `formatCalEvent` only reshapes what it receives; it cannot add members. Fix: extend the Prisma query to include the event type's team and hosts, then populate `team: { id, name, members }` when `booking.eventType?.teamId` is set.

- When an attendee or team admin adds a guest, the calendar update runs under that caller's credentials rather than the organizer's, so the provider call targets calendars the caller may not own. Lines 140-144 already target `booking.user.destinationCalendar`, and `booking.user.credentials` is eager-loaded at line 38 and then never used, which is the mismatch. Fix: build `EventManager` from `booking.user`. This is the same edit as #19 and #23 -- do it once.

- If the calendar provider is down, the guests are already in the database, the calendar is never updated, no email is sent, and the user's retry is permanently rejected with `emails_must_be_unique_valid` (the new guests are now existing attendees). There is no path back to a consistent state from the UI. Two options: catch and log the sync failure so it is non-fatal and the emails still go out, returning a partial-success flag; or delete the just-created attendee rows before rethrowing so the retry works. The first matches how the adjacent email call is already treated.

- An existing attendee whose address is resubmitted receives a full re-invite instead of the add-guests notice. Line 168 passes the raw `guests` input; `email-manager.ts:541` branches on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`, so anyone filtered out by the dedupe is still classified as new. Fix: `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, uniqueGuests);`.

- A total mail-delivery failure is invisible: the `catch` binds `err`, discards it, logs a static string via `console.log`, and line 173 still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. Operators get no signal and the user is told it worked. Fix: `logger.error("Error sending AddGuestsEmails", { bookingId, guests: uniqueGuests, err })` and surface the failure in the response.

- Umbrella coverage finding. 15 files, 555 insertions, zero test or spec files, across a new authorization matrix, a new filtering step, a calendar sync, four email templates, and a new shared UI component. Three files close the gap: a handler test covering the five-row authorization matrix and the dedupe/blocklist filter, a `MultiEmail.test.tsx`, and a Playwright spec for the dialog. The specific scenarios are enumerated in Coverage -> Testing gaps.

- Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, and finished bookings, and each one receives a `status: "CONFIRMED"` ICS invite. The lookup at lines 26-29 predicates only on `id`. `BookingListItem.tsx:553-554` also renders the new `add_members` action for past bookings. Fix: constrain the query with `status: { notIn: [CANCELLED, REJECTED] }`, reject past `endTime`, and filter the action out of the past-booking menu.

- A team ADMIN who is not the owner is denied. Lines 46-48 combine the two checks with `&&`, so the variable named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is true only for owners. The `?? 0` fallback also queries membership against nonexistent team id 0 on every personal booking. Fix: `const teamId = booking.eventType?.teamId; const isTeamAdminOrOwner = teamId != null && ((await isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId)) || (await isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId)));`.

- `Spam@Example.com` bypasses a blocklist containing `spam@example.com`, and `ALICE@example.com` creates a second attendee row alongside `alice@example.com`. Line 71 lowercases the blocklist but lines 74-78 compare the raw `guest` on both the blocklist and the existing-attendee check. The list side is also never trimmed, so `"a@x.com, b@x.com"` leaves a leading space on every entry after the first. Fix: normalize with `.trim().toLowerCase()` on both sides and persist the normalized address.

- A direct API call with the same address twice creates two attendee rows and two invites. `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29` refines for uniqueness client-side, but `addGuests.schema.ts:5` does not, and the handler's filter compares each guest only against stored attendees, never against the rest of the payload. A client-side check is not a server-side invariant. Fix: move the refine into the shared schema, then delete the local copy in the dialog and import the shared one so the two cannot drift again.

- After a failed submit, the validation banner survives a successful add and reappears on the next open of an empty form. `onSuccess` resets `multiEmailValue` but not `isInvalidEmail`; only the Cancel button resets it, and the dialog is mounted unconditionally by `BookingListItem.tsx:357-361`. Fix: `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` at the top of `handleAdd` and in `onSuccess`.

- The toast shows `FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission` to end users. `const message = ${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` is always a non-empty string, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback on line 44 can never fire and the newly added string is dead. Fix: fall back explicitly when `err.data?.code` is absent, and drop the code prefix to match the sibling handlers at `BookingListItem.tsx:702` and `:810`.

- `data-testid="add_members"` on the dialog confirm button collides with `id: "add_members"` on the dropdown action in the same rendered tree, so the first Playwright locator against it matches two elements and fails strict mode. Fix: rename the dialog hook to `add_guests_confirm` and the action to `add_guests` before any spec is written. (The missing spec itself is recorded under Testing gaps, folded into #8.)

- Confirmed by grep of `apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json`: `you_do_not_have_permission` has no entry, while `dont_have_permission` exists at line 1628 and both other keys this handler throws resolve. Fix: throw `dont_have_permission`, or add the new key alongside the six this diff already adds.

- A booking with a null `userId` produces an unhandled Prisma not-found (a 500) instead of the clean `TRPCError` used at line 44, and it happens after the authorization gate has already passed. No user row has id 0, so the `|| 0` coercion cannot succeed -- and the coercion is itself the evidence that `userId` is nullable. Fix: guard `booking.user` and drop the sentinel. Same edit as #4 and #23.

- Non-English users see an English tooltip. The component already calls `useLocale()` at line 13 and translates its sibling label via `t("add_another")` at line 69, so this one string escapes i18n. Fix: `t("remove_email")` plus the key.

- The handler re-queries the organizer whose row is already eager-loaded at lines 35-40, and includes `credentials: true` that is never read because line 158 uses `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` instead. Resolve together with #4 and #19 by deleting the query and using a guarded `booking.user`.

- `MultiEmail.tsx:2` imports from the `@calcom/ui` barrel that `index.tsx:153` re-exports it through, so the lazy chunk pulls the whole barrel back in -- defeating the "these are like 40kb" rationale in `MultiEmailLazy.tsx:3` -- and the self-referential edge can resolve to `undefined` under SSR or Jest. Fix: import the four components from their own modules. Advisory: two reviewers agreed, but neither could confirm whether barrel self-import is already house convention in `packages/ui` (siblings absent from the checkout).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — `guests[]` has no size bound and the mutation has no rate limit

adjudication.rationale: The schema does define `guests` as an unbounded `z.array(z.string().email())`, so it’s true there is no explicit max length in the diff. However, the finding also asserts “the mutation has no rate limit,” which is not verifiable from the diff: rate limiting could be applied inside `authedProcedure`, router middleware, API gateway, or other shared infrastructure not shown here. Because the claim combines a verifiable observation with an unverified assertion (and the lack of a size bound is a policy/perf concern rather than a definite defect), the finding as stated is not a strictly verifiable problem in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - One authenticated request can create an unbounded number of attendee rows and send an unbounded number of emails from the Cal.com sending domain. `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` declares neither `.min()` nor `.max()`, and no `checkRateLimitAndThrowError` guards the procedure. Any user who is merely an attendee on a booking can drive it. The cost is domain-reputation damage and a provider-side attendee-cap rejection on the calendar side. Fix: `.min(1).max(10)` on the schema plus a per-user rate limit. The cap value is a product choice -- 10 is the reviewers' defensible default; tune it to whatever booking creation already allows. Severity note: security called this P0, performance and adversarial called it P1. Kept at P0 because the fix is two lines and the abuse path needs no privilege beyond being on the invite.

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.min()`/`.max()` bound in `addGuests.schema.ts`, and the handler uses `createMany` to insert one attendee row per (filtered) guest email with no additional cap. It then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which iterates over `calendarEvent.attendees` and enqueues an email per attendee (plus organizer/team-member emails), so a single request can trigger a very large number of DB inserts and outbound emails. The procedure is `authedProcedure` and explicitly allows any existing attendee (`isAttendee`) to perform the action, so the abuse path does not require organizer/admin privileges. There is no rate-limit guard shown in the diff for this endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:124 — `evt` omits `team`, so the team-member email loop never runs

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the constructed CalendarEvent `evt` includes organizer, attendees, etc., but does not include any `team` field (nor is any team data fetched/attached). In email-manager.ts, sendAddGuestsEmails calls `formatCalEvent(calEvent)` and then only emails team members inside `if (calendarEvent.team?.members) { ... }`. With `evt.team` omitted, `calendarEvent.team` will be falsy unless `formatCalEvent` somehow synthesizes team + members (not shown in this diff and generally unlikely), so the team-member loop will not execute and team members won’t receive the organizer notification email.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — Calendar sync uses the caller's credentials, not the booking owner's

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler fetches the booking including `user.credentials` (the booking owner/organizer’s connected calendar credentials), but then builds `EventManager` with `ctx.user` (the caller) and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. Since the caller can be an attendee or team member (`isAttendee` / team admin path), the calendar update (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`) will use the caller’s credentials rather than the booking owner’s, which is a correctness issue and can cause calendar sync to fail or target the wrong account.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — Calendar-sync failure leaves guests committed, unsynced, and un-retryable

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code first persists new attendees via prisma.booking.update(...attendees.createMany...) and only afterwards calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking). If updateCalendarAttendees throws, the mutation will fail but the guests are already committed in the DB (no transaction/rollback shown). A subsequent retry of the mutation will compute uniqueGuests by filtering out existing booking.attendees, resulting in uniqueGuests.length===0 and a BAD_REQUEST, so the calendar sync is effectively not retryable through this endpoint.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: the code deciding which email type to send bases the routing on the raw input guests list (e.g., `newGuests`/`guests`) rather than the actual/persisted attendee set (e.g., `calendarEvent.attendees`/`uniqueGuests`). adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:169 — Email-send failure is swallowed; the mutation still reports success

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email step is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and then the handler unconditionally returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. This means any failure in `sendAddGuestsEmails` is swallowed (no rethrow / no error response), so the mutation reports success even when email delivery fails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44 — No booking status or time guard before mutating and re-inviting

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler`, after fetching the booking by `id`, the code proceeds to compute permissions and then unconditionally `prisma.booking.update(...)` to add attendees and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)` / `sendAddGuestsEmails(...)`. There is no check against booking lifecycle state (e.g., cancelled) or temporal validity (e.g., booking already ended / started) despite `booking.startTime`/`endTime` being available in the fetched record and later used to build the `CalendarEvent`. This means guests can be added and invitations/emails can be sent for past or otherwise non-modifiable bookings, which is a concrete correctness/behavior issue in this diff.

The handler also does not dedupe duplicates within the incoming `guests` array (it only filters out existing attendees/blacklisted), so a caller can bypass the client and submit duplicate emails, potentially creating duplicate attendees and/or triggering downstream issues (duplicate calendar updates/emails/DB constraints).

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the provider update is executed using the caller’s session user, not the booking organizer: it does `const { user } = ctx;` then `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and constructs `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`, finally calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. The booking query eagerly includes `user: { ... credentials: true }` (organizer credentials) but those are never used. This creates a concrete mismatch when a non-organizer (attendee / team admin) invokes the mutation: the calendar update will attempt to run under the caller’s credentials rather than the organizer’s, which is a correctness defect and can cause updates to target calendars the caller owns (or fail to update the organizer’s calendar).

adjudication_records.issue_text: - If the calendar provider is down, the guests are already in the database, the calendar is never updated, no email is sent, and the user's retry is permanently rejected with `emails_must_be_unique_valid` (the new guests are now existing attendees). There is no path back to a consistent state from the UI. Two options: catch and log the sync failure so it is non-fatal and the emails still go out, returning a partial-success flag; or delete the just-created attendee rows before rethrowing so the retry works. The first matches how the adjacent email call is already treated.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuestsHandler`, the code first persists the new guests via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no `try/catch` or transaction. If the calendar update throws (e.g., provider outage), the mutation fails after the DB write, leaving attendees added in the database but no calendar sync and no emails (because `sendAddGuestsEmails` is after the calendar update and won’t run). A subsequent retry will likely compute `uniqueGuests` as empty because those emails now exist in `booking.attendees`, triggering `BAD_REQUEST` with `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, so the UI has no straightforward way to reach a consistent state. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - An existing attendee whose address is resubmitted receives a full re-invite instead of the add-guests notice. Line 168 passes the raw `guests` input; `email-manager.ts:541` branches on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`, so anyone filtered out by the dedupe is still classified as new. Fix: `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, uniqueGuests);`.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB update and `guestsFullDetails` are based on `uniqueGuests` (filtered to exclude existing attendees and blacklisted emails). However, the email call uses the raw `guests` input: `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);`. In `email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` decides whether an attendee gets a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` by checking `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`. If a user re-submits an email that is already an attendee, it will be excluded from `uniqueGuests` (so not actually “new”), but it remains in `guests`, causing that existing attendee to match `includes(...)` and receive the full scheduled/re-invite email. Passing `uniqueGuests` would align the email classification with who was actually added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - A total mail-delivery failure is invisible: the `catch` binds `err`, discards it, logs a static string via `console.log`, and line 173 still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. Operators get no signal and the user is told it worked. Fix: `logger.error("Error sending AddGuestsEmails", { bookingId, guests: uniqueGuests, err })` and surface the failure in the response.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and the handler then returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` unconditionally. The caught `err` is discarded and only a static `console.log` is emitted, so an email-delivery failure is not propagated and lacks actionable logging context (no error details, bookingId, or guest list). This is a verifiable defect in the diff (swallowed error + inadequate logging).

adjudication_records.issue_text: - Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, and finished bookings, and each one receives a `status: "CONFIRMED"` ICS invite. The lookup at lines 26-29 predicates only on `id`. `BookingListItem.tsx:553-554` also renders the new `add_members` action for past bookings. adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts` the booking is fetched with `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })` and there is no subsequent check on booking status (cancelled/rejected) or on `endTime`/time-in-past before mutating attendees and sending emails. The new email templates also hardcode `status: "CONFIRMED"` in the generated ICS payloads (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`), so if guests are added to a cancelled/rejected/past booking they would still receive a confirmed invite. On the UI side, the new `add_members` action is appended to `bookingMenuItems` unconditionally in `BookingListItem.tsx`, with no visible gating by booking status or whether the booking is in the past, so it can be shown for past/cancelled bookings as well.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - A team ADMIN who is not the owner is denied. Lines 46-48 combine the two checks with `&&`, so the variable named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is true only for owners. The `?? 0` fallback also queries membership against nonexistent team id 0 on every personal booking. Fix: `const teamId = booking.eventType?.teamId; const isTeamAdminOrOwner = teamId != null && ((await isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId)) || (await isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId)));`.
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the permission check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, which wrongly requires both to be true and denies admins who aren't owners. It recommends using || so either role grants permission, matching the golden issue (extra note about ??0 is additional but doesn't change the core match).

adjudication_records.issue_text: - `Spam@Example.com` bypasses a blocklist containing `spam@example.com`, and `ALICE@example.com` creates a second attendee row alongside `alice@example.com`. Line 71 lowercases the blocklist but lines 74-78 compare the raw `guest` on both the blocklist and the existing-attendee check. The list side is also never trimmed, so `"a@x.com, b@x.com"` leaves a leading space on every entry after the first. Fix: normalize with `.trim().toLowerCase()` on both sides and persist the normalized address.
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate explicitly describes that the blocklist is lowercased but the incoming `guest` email is compared in its raw form, allowing uppercase variants (e.g., `Spam@Example.com`) to bypass `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. That is the same underlying bypass issue described in the golden comment, though the candidate also adds related normalization/duplicate-attendee concerns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - A direct API call with the same address twice creates two attendee rows and two invites. `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29` refines for uniqueness client-side, but `addGuests.schema.ts:5` does not, and the handler's filter compares each guest only against stored attendees, never against the rest of the payload. A client-side check is not a server-side invariant. Fix: move the refine into the shared schema, then delete the local copy in the dialog and import the shared one so the two cannot drift again.
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes that submitting the same email twice in the payload results in two attendee rows/invites because the server-side schema/handler only filters against existing attendees, not duplicates within the incoming list, and client-side uniqueness isn’t enforced server-side. adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:36 — `isInvalidEmail` banner is never cleared on success

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43 — Error-toast fallback is unreachable and the toast leaks the raw tRPC code

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx the onError handler builds `message` via a template literal: ``const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;``. Template literals always produce a (truthy) string, even when `err.data?.code` is undefined (yielding e.g. `"undefined: ..."`). Therefore `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), ...)` will never hit the fallback branch, making it effectively unreachable. Also, the toast explicitly prefixes the user-facing message with the raw tRPC error code (`err.data?.code`), which will be displayed to end users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:58 — Booking with null `userId` reaches `findFirstOrThrow` via the `\

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer lookup uses `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. adjudication_records.issue_text: - A booking with a null `userId` produces an unhandled Prisma not-found (a 500) instead of the clean `TRPCError` used at line 44, and it happens after the authorization gate has already passed. No user row has id 0, so the `|| 0` coercion cannot succeed -- and the coercion is itself the evidence that `userId` is nullable. Fix: guard `booking.user` and drop the sentinel. adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, after loading `booking`, the code unconditionally does `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } ... })`. The `|| 0` is a sentinel that only makes sense if `booking.userId` can be `null/undefined`, and if it is null, the query becomes `id: 0`, which will not match a real user and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw. That error is not converted to a `TRPCError` (unlike the earlier `if (!booking) throw new TRPCError(...)`), so it will surface as an internal error/500. This can happen even when the authorization gate passes (e.g., `isAttendee` is true), because the organizer lookup happens after the permission check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: - `MultiEmail.tsx:2` imports from the `@calcom/ui` barrel that `index.tsx:153` re-exports it through, so the lazy chunk pulls the whole barrel back in -- defeating the "these are like 40kb" rationale in `MultiEmailLazy.tsx:3` -- and the self-referential edge can resolve to `undefined` under SSR or Jest. adjudication.rationale: Yes: the diff introduces a verifiable circular/self-referential dependency and likely defeats the intended code-splitting. `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx` imports `{ Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip }` from `@calcom/ui` (the package barrel). That barrel (`packages/ui/index.tsx`) now re-exports `MultiEmail` via `./form/MultiEmailLazy`, and `MultiEmailLazy.tsx` dynamically imports `./MultiEmail`. So the lazy-loaded `MultiEmail` chunk depends on the barrel that (transitively) points back to the lazy entry, creating a cycle (`MultiEmail -> @calcom/ui(index) -> MultiEmailLazy -> import('./MultiEmail')`). Independently of whether it always breaks at runtime, importing the barrel from within a lazily loaded module is very likely to pull the barrel (and its transitive exports) into the lazy chunk, undermining the “these are like 40kb” rationale. This is grounded entirely in the shown imports/exports in the diff.
